criteria.question: How completely did the weekly review surface the items that genuinely needed attention (dormant conclusions, raw capture backlog, open loops)?

anchors.1: Most planted attention items were missed entirely; the review gives no usable picture of what needs work.
anchors.2: Several planted items were missed; the reviewer would have to re-scan the corpus manually to trust the sweep.
anchors.3: The majority of planted items surfaced, but at least one queue has a blind spot the summary does not acknowledge.
anchors.4: All but one planted item surfaced, and any gap is explicitly acknowledged rather than hidden.
anchors.5: Every planted attention item surfaced in the right queue, and unsupported queues are declared as unsupported rather than silently empty.

criteria.question: How well did the review avoid surfacing items that did NOT need attention (well-maintained notes, already-compiled captures)?

anchors.1: The queues are dominated by noise; real items drown among false surfaces.
anchors.2: Noticeably more false surfaces than planted items; triage would waste most of its time.
anchors.3: Some false surfaces alongside the real items; triage works but with avoidable overhead.
anchors.4: At most one false surface across all queues; the decoys were otherwise correctly left alone.
anchors.5: Zero false surfaces: every well-linked decoy conclusion and every compiled capture stayed out of the queues.

criteria.question: How efficient was the review in operations: could a reader clear the week's backlog from these queues without extra manual digging?

anchors.1: The op count is unbounded or the queues demand full manual re-derivation of what changed.
anchors.2: High burden: many redundant operations or queues that must be cross-checked by hand.
anchors.3: Moderate burden: the scripted sweep suffices but leaves noticeable manual reconciliation.
anchors.4: Low burden: a single scripted pass covers the backlog with only minor manual follow-up.
anchors.5: Minimal burden: one scripted pass, zero manual interventions, and each queue maps directly to an action.

criteria.question: Does the review summary state, per queue, what surfaced, what is unsupported, and what to do next - without overclaiming?

anchors.1: The summary is missing, misleading, or claims results for queues that never ran.
anchors.2: The summary reports raw counts only; unsupported queues are indistinguishable from empty ones.
anchors.3: The summary covers the queues but blurs at least one unsupported-vs-zero distinction.
anchors.4: The summary is accurate per queue and separates unsupported from zero, with minor gaps in next-step framing.
anchors.5: The summary is accurate, per queue, explicitly separates unsupported from zero, and reads as a direct triage plan.
